What the official code does

  1. Load audio.wav, check 100 kHz and 2 channels, scale int16 to float64 by 1/32768.
  2. Band-pass each mic channel once per transmitter with a 5th-order Butterworth (scipy.signal.butter + lfilter, causal, single pass): 17.5–28.5 kHz for speaker 0, 28.5–39.5 kHz for speaker 1. Result: 2 tx × 2 mics signals.
  3. Chirp alignment: cross-correlate each filtered signal with its transmitted chirp (tx_signals/*.wav, 500 samples) over the whole file (cap 50 M samples), fold the correlation into 500-sample frames, average |corr| over all frames and paths, and take the argmax. The audio is then trimmed by start_pos = (argmax + 250) mod 500, which puts the strongest echo, the direct path, at bin 250.
  4. Framing: drop the trailing partial frame and reshape to (2, 2, n_frames, 500). Frame f covers samples start_pos + 500f … +500.
  5. Echo profile: for every frame, np.correlate(frame, chirp, 'full')[499:], i.e. the correlation at lags 0…499 within the frame (no wrap-around across frame edges). Output float64.
  6. Differential profile (in main()): |p[t]| − |p[t−1]| along time, zero-padded at t = 0.
  7. No normalisation of profiles. PNG plots clip raw profiles to [0, 5] and diffs to [−0.1, 0.1].
  8. main() processes only SoniSpeech_silent_eval as shipped and writes full float64 arrays into the dataset folders. Do not run it over the dataset; scripts/preprocess.py should import calculate_echo_profiles as this EDA does.

Frame alignment for cutting utterances

start_frame = floor((start_s·100000 − start_pos) / 500), end_frame = ceil((end_s·100000 − start_pos) / 500). Ignoring start_pos shifts cuts by up to one frame (5 ms).
